description: ORBITRAX is a team from Dadu, Pakistan, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We combine technology, creativity, and NASA Earth observation data to build practical solutions for real-world challenges.
summary: FarmShift helps farmers compare crop rotation options using real NASA climate data and a live weather forecast, and explains why one option fits their farm better than the others.
details:
Farmers today are not short of crop choices. What they lack is an easy way to compare those choices when the weather keeps changing. Rainfall comes late, summers run hotter, and water is not always there when you need it. We wanted to build something that takes that confusion and turns it into a clear, explainable answer.

With FarmShift, you tell the app where your farm is, what kind of soil you have, how much water you can count on, and what matters most to you, whether that’s saving water, protecting the soil or handling heat. The app then pulls real temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind and solar data from NASA for that exact location, shows you the area on a satellite map, and scores four rotation strategies against those conditions. You don’t just get a number. You get the reasoning behind it, so you can see why a rotation ranks first.

Technologies used

NASA POWER API for climate data

NASA GIBS (MODIS imagery) for satellite context

Open-Meteo API for the 16-day forecast and crop water demand

Google Maps and OpenStreetMap for location search and maps

HTML, CSS and JavaScript

Chart.js for the charts and Leaflet for the satellite map

How we used NASA data\

NASA POWER gives us the last twelve months of temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind and solar radiation for the chosen location. NASA GIBS provides MODIS satellite imagery so the analysis stays connected to a real place on Earth. This data drives the rotation scoring and the evidence the app shows.

Impact\

FarmShift is meant for small and mid-size farmers, agronomy students and advisors, and anyone working in a water-stressed region. It makes climate data easier to act on without needing a specialist.

Limitations (we are upfront about these)\

FarmShift is a comparison and decision-support tool. It does not predict yields. NASA data gives the climate context, and the crop scoring uses simplified crop characteristics, so it should support a decision rather than replace local agronomic advice.

What we would build next\

More crops and regions, richer NASA data such as soil moisture and vegetation indices, and support for Urdu and other local languages with a mobile-friendly mode.
